# function: port_spec

Parses a `docker run -p` port spec, `[host_ip:][host_port:]container_port[/protocol]`, into `host_ip`, `host_port`, `container_port` and `protocol`. IPv6 host addresses go in brackets (`[::1]:8080:80`), ports may be ranges (`8000-8010:80-90`), and the protocol defaults to `tcp`. Absent host parts are empty strings; an invalid spec is an error.

Provider functions require Terraform 1.8 or later and are called as
`provider::docker::port_spec(...)`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
locals {
  p = provider::docker::port_spec("127.0.0.1:8080:80/tcp")
  # p = { host_ip = "127.0.0.1", host_port = "8080", container_port = "80", protocol = "tcp" }

  v6 = provider::docker::port_spec("[::1]:5353:53/udp")
  # v6.host_ip = "::1", v6.protocol = "udp"

  range = provider::docker::port_spec("8000-8010:80-90")
  # range.host_port = "8000-8010", range.container_port = "80-90"
}

output "published_port" {
  value = tonumber(local.p.host_port)
}
```

## Signature

<!-- signature generated by tfplugindocs -->
```text
port_spec(spec string) object
```

## Arguments

<!-- arguments generated by tfplugindocs -->
1. `spec` (String) Port spec, e.g. `8080:80`, `127.0.0.1:53:53/udp` or `[::1]:8443:443`.
